Paradise Bay, also known as Paradise Harbour, lies off the Danco Coast of the Antarctic Peninsula. It is bordered by the mainland to the east and south, Lemaire Island to the north and Bryde Island to the west. This setting creates alternating views of islands and the continental shore as a vessel moves through the bay.

The Belgian Antarctic Expedition first mapped the bay's approximate outlines in February 1898. Whalers continued exploring the area in the early twentieth century and are also associated with the name Paradise Harbour. Today, visits to the bay focus on the seascape and ice-bound shores; the expedition team determines which parts of the route are accessible and whether boat excursions are possible.

## Ballestas Islands and sea lions: what to see on the Paracas Peninsula

The Paracas Peninsula is a jewel of Peru's Pacific coast. Cliffs shaped into unusual forms by wind and seawater, together with numerous colonies of sea lions and cormorants, are only some of the area's attractions.

## Holidays on the Paracas Peninsula

### What makes Paracas so appealing?

The mysterious markings in the valley known as the Nazca Lines are even more famous. Less than 300 kilometers south of the Peruvian capital, semidesert gives way to a true desert. Ocean waves crash against bare cliffs devoid of vegetation. The steep Paracas coast is full of remarkable grottos and narrow stretches of land. Sandy hills offer ample opportunities for dune surfing. Nature enthusiasts enjoy traveling by motorboat to the Ballestas Islands to watch sea lions. The rocky ocean coastline also provides an excellent resting place for migratory birds. Pelicans, fulmars, Peruvian cormorants and Chilean flamingos can all be seen here.

### Paramaribo — Suriname's vibrant city!

Paramaribo is the liveliest and most colorful city in Suriname. Black-and-white Dutch colonial buildings alternate with grassy squares lined with shops, cafes, restaurants and nightclubs.

## Visiting Paramaribo

### Paramaribo — Suriname's multicultural city!

The Maron district, comparable to Montmartre, is an open-air art exhibition where local artists sell colorful paintings. Paramaribo is a multiethnic city. Mosques and synagogues stand side by side, with Catholic churches nearby. In 2002, the historic part of the city was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. Paramaribo has numerous parks offering cool shade even in the hottest weather. The riverbanks are lined with mangrove forests.

Paraty combines a historic town with the natural scenery of Brazil's Atlantic coast. Its colonial center, with cobblestone streets, white buildings and churches, recalls the era when the port was connected to the Gold Trail.


Paraty's historic center is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property "Paraty and Ilha Grande – Culture and Biodiversity." Yet a visit here extends beyond architecture. From the town, it is easy to head out into the bay toward islands and beaches, while the surrounding area offers waterfalls and nature trails.


A separate day can be devoted to Trindade, with its beaches and fishing heritage. Paraty fits naturally into an itinerary between Rio de Janeiro and other stops along the Green Coast, especially for travelers who want a slower pace that brings culture and the sea together.
